# Implementation Plan: Codex marketplace-index policy schema guard (D-001)
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-marketplace-parse-robustness"} -->


*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-05. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-marketplace-parse-robustness/plan.md`.*
*Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/codex-marketplace-parse-robustness/selected-direction.md` (direction D-001).*

## Overview

A `policy.authentication: "OFF"` value shipped in our codex marketplace index on 2026-06-05 made
codex abort the *entire* index parse — codex's `core-plugins/src/marketplace.rs` does a single
all-or-nothing `serde_json::from_str`, and its two policy enums use `#[serde(rename)]` with **no**
`#[serde(other)]`, so one unknown enum value invalidates every plugin in the file. The only surfaced
symptom was the masked TUI string `Failed to add marketplace.`

This plan adds a **producer-side schema guard** living entirely in the `ai-developer-toolkit` repo
that validates every marketplace-index entry's `policy` enum values against codex's accepted enum
sets **before a plugin release ships**, so that exact failure can never be released again. It is the
ZERO-codex-conflict-surface direction (D-001): **no edits under `codex/`**. Per the operator's
2026-06-05 decision, the codex-side directions D-002 (partial-parse), D-003 (TUI error surfacing),
and D-004 (tolerant enum) are explicitly **dropped**.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
- **Three marketplace indexes** in `ai-developer-toolkit/` (researcher + codex, corroborated):
  - `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` — the **codex** index; the only one that carries a
    `policy:{installation,authentication}` object per entry. **All 14 entries today are
    `AVAILABLE` / `ON_INSTALL`** (no bad values currently shipped).
  - `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `.github/plugin/marketplace.json` — minimal installer
    schema (`name`, `source`, `description`, `version`); **no `policy` object**.
- **Release gate:** `.claude/skills/release-plugin/SKILL.md` Pre-flight (lines ~35-75) = 3 steps:
  clean-tree check, monotonic-semver check, confirm-plugin-in-all-3-indexes (`jq`). It bumps the
  three indexes with `jq`. Line ~191 currently asserts "It does not run tests." This skill is the
  single gate every version bump flows through, but it is **instruction-only markdown** — to get
  enforcement teeth it must shell out to an executable validator.
- **Test convention:** plain Node, **no framework**, **no root `package.json`** anywhere in the
  repo. Per-plugin tests are `*.test.js` run by `plugins/crews/tests/run.js` (a worker-thread
  runner) with local `require('./lib/assert')` helpers and fixtures under `tests/fixtures/`.
- **No CI:** `ai-developer-toolkit/.github/` contains only `acl/`, `copilot/`, `plugin/` — there is
  **no `.github/workflows/`**. So the release-plugin Pre-flight is the only *enforcement* point that
  exists today; a standalone validator is the reusable engine and the future-CI / pre-commit seam.
- **Codex enum ground truth** (verified directly from
  `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/marketplace.rs`):
  - `MarketplacePluginInstallPolicy` (~lines 90-99): `NOT_AVAILABLE`, `AVAILABLE`, `INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT`.
  - `MarketplacePluginAuthPolicy` (~lines 101-108): `ON_INSTALL`, `ON_USE`.
  - Both derive `Default` and use `#[serde(default)]` on the policy fields, so a **missing** policy
    field/object is valid; only an out-of-set **value** aborts the parse.

### Technical Constraints
- **Toolkit-only:** zero edits under `codex/`. The guard couples to codex's enums by *mirroring*
  them in one toolkit-owned constant, with a comment citing `marketplace.rs`.
- Dependency-free Node, runnable with a bare `node` invocation (no install step, no framework).
- Windows host: use `node:fs` + `node:path`, no POSIX-separator assumptions.
- Must tolerate the two policy-free indexes (validating them must not error merely because they lack
  `policy`).

## Approach

### Architecture
A single dependency-free ESM module is the **one engine** reused by both placements:

1. **Validator module + CLI** — `tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.mjs`:
   - Exports a frozen single-source-of-truth constant:
     ```js
     // Mirror of codex's accepted marketplace policy enums.
     // SOURCE OF TRUTH: codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/marketplace.rs
     //   MarketplacePluginInstallPolicy (~L90-99) + MarketplacePluginAuthPolicy (~L101-108).
     // If codex changes these enums, update THIS constant (one-line edit) to match.
     export const CODEX_MARKETPLACE_POLICY_ENUMS = {
       installation: ['NOT_AVAILABLE', 'AVAILABLE', 'INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT'],
       authentication: ['ON_INSTALL', 'ON_USE'],
     };
     ```
   - Exports `validateMarketplaceFile(filePath)` → returns a list of violation objects
     (`{ file, pluginName, fieldPath, badValue, accepted }`); and `validateFiles(paths)` aggregating
     across files. A thin CLI entry (run when invoked directly via
     `import.meta.url === ... process.argv` guard) accepts one-or-more file paths (defaulting to the
     three indexes), prints each violation to stderr, and exits `1` if any, else `0`.
   - **Validation rule (critical):** for each `.plugins[]` entry:
     - A **missing** `policy` object, or a present `policy` object missing an individual field, is
       **VALID** (mirrors codex `#[serde(default)]`). This is what makes the two policy-free indexes
       pass cleanly — it is the #1 correctness requirement.
     - A `policy` that is **present but not a plain object** (`null`, an array, a string like `"OFF"`,
       a number) is a **violation** — codex deserializes `policy` as a struct, so a non-object value
       would also abort its parse. (Codex review finding F-002.)
     - When `policy` is a plain object, each of `installation` / `authentication` that is **present**
       must be a **string in** the corresponding accepted set; a non-string or out-of-set value is a
       violation.
   - **Error message** matches the codex CLI's clarity, e.g.:
     `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json: plugins[<name>].policy.authentication: unknown variant "OFF", expected one of: ON_INSTALL, ON_USE`
     (when an entry lacks `name`, fall back to `plugins[<index>]`). Collect and print **all**
     violations before exiting, not just the first.
   - Distinguish *file/JSON* errors (missing file, unparseable JSON) from *policy* violations with a
     distinct message + non-zero exit, so a malformed index isn't silently treated as "no violations".

2. **Fixtures + self-test** — `tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.test.mjs` (self-running; uses
   `node:assert`, exits non-zero on failure — needs no external runner), with
   `tools/fixtures/marketplace-policy-valid.json` and
   `tools/fixtures/marketplace-policy-invalid-auth-off.json`.

3. **Enforcement wiring** — add a Pre-flight step to `release-plugin/SKILL.md` that runs the CLI
   against the three indexes and aborts on non-zero, **before** any version-file edits (so a
   pre-existing bad value blocks the release immediately, exactly as 2026-06-05 would have been).

**Placement decision:** the validator lives at the **repo-level `tools/` directory**, NOT inside
`plugins/crews/`. Both Explore agents suggested nesting it under `plugins/crews/` solely to reuse
that plugin's `run.js` runner; that is rejected — a repo-wide *release gate* must not live inside an
unrelated plugin, and a self-running `.test.mjs` needs no external runner. Codex's independent
research reached the same `tools/` conclusion. `tools/` is an existing repo-level directory
(`tools/teams-sync`, `tools/build-tools.sh`, etc.), so this fits the established layout.

### Implementation Strategy
1. Build the validator module + CLI first (the engine everything else depends on).
2. Add fixtures + the self-test; prove FAIL-on-bad / PASS-on-good / PASS-on-real-index.
3. Wire the CLI into release-plugin Pre-flight and update docs.
4. **Ship via the two-commit submodule flow (Codex review finding F-001, Critical):** all edits land
   as a commit *inside* the `ai-developer-toolkit/` submodule first; codexu then records the updated
   `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule-pointer as a **separate codexu commit**. Per codexu `AGENTS.md`
   ("Submodule edits require two commits"), the pointer bump is the lead/bookkeeper ship step — the
   impl member commits inside the toolkit worktree; do NOT stage unrelated parent changes. Without
   the pointer bump, codexu does not actually consume the guard.

### Files to Create/Modify
**Create** (all under `ai-developer-toolkit/`):
- `tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.mjs` — SoT enum constant + validation engine + CLI.
- `tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.test.mjs` — self-running plain-Node test.
- `tools/fixtures/marketplace-policy-valid.json` — minimal valid index (policy AVAILABLE/ON_INSTALL).
- `tools/fixtures/marketplace-policy-invalid-auth-off.json` — same but one entry `authentication: "OFF"`.
- `tools/fixtures/marketplace-policy-invalid-installation.json` — one entry with an out-of-set
  `installation` value (covers the installation path; Codex + Claude review finding F-005).

**Modify** (all under `ai-developer-toolkit/`):
- `.claude/skills/release-plugin/SKILL.md` — new Pre-flight step invoking the CLI + abort-on-nonzero;
  reconcile the line ~191 "does not run tests" wording (clarify it runs a fast schema *guard*, not
  the plugin test suite).
- `AGENTS.md` — add a sentence in the "keep the marketplace indexes in sync" section pointing at the
  new guard + that release-plugin enforces it.
- `docs/codex-plugins-local.md` — document the policy-value guard and the `marketplace.rs` coupling.

## Scope

### In Scope
- A single toolkit-owned validator (engine + CLI) with one SoT enum constant + `marketplace.rs`
  coupling comment.
- Validation of `policy.installation` / `policy.authentication` values across the codex index, while
  tolerating the two policy-free indexes (and any future entry that legitimately omits `policy`).
- Precise, codex-clarity violation messages (plugin id + field path + bad value + accepted set).
- Valid + invalid fixtures and a self-running test proving FAIL/PASS behavior and a non-brittle smoke
  pass against the real `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`.
- Wiring the guard into `release-plugin` Pre-flight (enforcement teeth) and the standalone-runnable
  CLI (future CI / pre-commit seam).
- Doc updates (release-plugin SKILL.md, root AGENTS.md, docs/codex-plugins-local.md).
- Shipping via the **two-commit submodule flow**: the change is committed inside
  `ai-developer-toolkit/`, and codexu records the updated submodule pointer as a separate commit
  (the lead/bookkeeper ship step).

### Out of Scope (operator-dropped)
- **D-002** codex partial-parse (upstream OR fork); **D-003** TUI error surfacing; **D-004** tolerant
  `#[serde(other)]` enum. No edits under `codex/`.
- Robustness for **third-party** marketplaces a codex user might add (the guard only protects indexes
  WE publish).
- Cross-index entry name/version **sync** validation (release-plugin already checks presence-in-all-3;
  full parity checking is a separate concern, not the policy-value bug).
- New test framework, root `package.json`, husky/pre-commit infra, or a CI workflow (beyond making
  the CLI CI-ready).

## Risk Areas
- **#1 false-positive risk — missing `policy` must be VALID.** If the validator flags a *missing*
  `policy` object/field as invalid, it would reject the two policy-free indexes and break **every**
  release. The rule must validate values *only when present*. The self-test must include a
  policy-free index passing.
- **Brittle smoke assertion.** Asserting "exactly 14 entries" (as the agents suggested) breaks the
  moment a plugin is added. The smoke test should assert "≥1 codex-index entry carries `policy` AND
  all policy values are in-set ⇒ exit 0", not a hardcoded count, and must not assume `ON_INSTALL`
  specifically (only set-membership), since `ON_USE` / `INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT` are legitimately valid.
- **Field path when `name` is absent** — fall back to `plugins[<index>]`.
- **ESM vs CJS** — `.mjs` is ESM regardless of the missing `package.json`; the test imports the
  module via ESM `import`. (A CJS `.js` variant matching crews' tests is acceptable if the impl
  prefers; the plan recommends `.mjs` for zero ambiguity.)
- **Release-plugin cwd** — the Pre-flight command must use repo-root-relative paths; the skill runs
  from repo root.
- **Malformed-JSON vs violation** — keep these as distinct failures so a broken index isn't reported
  as "clean."
- **`policy` present but not an object** (`null`/`[]`/`"OFF"`/number) must be a violation, not
  silently skipped — codex deserializes `policy` as a struct (Codex review finding F-002).
- **Read `ai-developer-toolkit/tools/AGENTS.md` before adding files under `tools/`** (Codex review
  finding F-006). It is a developer-guide pointer file with no rule that blocks a plain-Node `.mjs`
  tool (the dir already holds mixed JS/shell/Python tooling), but the impl should confirm.
- **Submodule pointer bump must not be forgotten** (Codex review finding F-001) — see Implementation
  Strategy step 4; a toolkit-only commit without the codexu pointer bump means codexu never consumes
  the guard.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A single toolkit-owned constant defines codex's accepted policy enum sets
      (`installation ∈ {NOT_AVAILABLE, AVAILABLE, INSTALLED_BY_DEFAULT}`,
      `authentication ∈ {ON_INSTALL, ON_USE}`) with a comment citing `marketplace.rs`; changing the
      sets is a one-line edit in ONE place.
- [ ] `node tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.mjs .agents/plugins/marketplace.json .claude-plugin/marketplace.json .github/plugin/marketplace.json`
      run from the toolkit repo root **exits 0** against the current real indexes.
- [ ] Running the CLI against `tools/fixtures/marketplace-policy-invalid-auth-off.json` **exits
      non-zero** and prints a message naming the plugin id, the field path
      `plugins[<name>].policy.authentication`, the bad value `OFF`, and the accepted set
      (`ON_INSTALL`, `ON_USE`).
- [ ] Running the CLI against `tools/fixtures/marketplace-policy-valid.json` **exits 0**.
- [ ] Running the CLI against a policy-free index (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) **exits 0**
      (missing `policy` is not flagged).
- [ ] An out-of-set `installation` value is also caught, with the installation accepted set in the
      message, and is covered by a dedicated invalid fixture
      (`tools/fixtures/marketplace-policy-invalid-installation.json`).
- [ ] A `policy` that is PRESENT but not a plain object (`null`, `[]`, `"OFF"`, a number) is a
      violation (non-zero exit, names the plugin) — codex requires `policy` to deserialize as a
      struct, so a non-object `policy` would also abort its parse.
- [ ] A non-string `installation`/`authentication` value is rejected with the same precise field-path
      message as an out-of-set string.
- [ ] An entry with a bad policy value but no `name` field reports the field path as
      `plugins[<index>]` (index fallback).
- [ ] A malformed/unparseable index file (or a missing file path) fails with a non-zero exit and a
      message that is distinct from a policy violation (it must NOT be silently reported as "clean").
- [ ] Running the CLI against BOTH policy-free indexes (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` AND
      `.github/plugin/marketplace.json`) exits 0 (missing `policy` is not flagged).
- [ ] `node tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.test.mjs` exercises invalid-fail, valid-pass,
      policy-free-pass, and a non-brittle real-index smoke-pass; it runs with a bare `node`
      invocation (no framework, no `package.json`) and exits non-zero if any assertion fails.
- [ ] `release-plugin/SKILL.md` Pre-flight invokes the CLI against the three indexes and aborts the
      release on non-zero, before any version-file edits; the line ~191 "does not run tests" wording
      is reconciled.
- [ ] Docs updated: root `AGENTS.md` "keep indexes in sync" section + `docs/codex-plugins-local.md`
      reference the guard.
- [ ] **Zero changes under `codex/`** — the entire code/doc change set is inside `ai-developer-toolkit`.
- [ ] **Two-commit submodule contract:** toolkit changes are committed inside `ai-developer-toolkit/`,
      and codexu records the updated `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule pointer as a separate codexu
      commit, with no unrelated parent changes staged (Codex review finding F-001/F-004).

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- **US-001 — Validator module + CLI** (`tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.mjs`): SoT enum
  constant + coupling comment, value-validation engine (missing-policy-tolerant, all-violations,
  malformed-JSON distinct), multi-file CLI with codex-clarity errors. Verified by running against the
  real indexes (exit 0).
- **US-002 — Fixtures + self-test** (`tools/fixtures/*.json`, `tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.test.mjs`):
  invalid `authentication:"OFF"` fixture + invalid `installation` fixture + valid fixture; self-running
  test asserting auth-fail, installation-fail, non-object-`policy`-fail, missing-`name` index fallback,
  malformed-JSON distinct failure, valid-pass, BOTH policy-free indexes pass, and a non-brittle
  real-index smoke (set-membership, not a hardcoded count). Depends on US-001.
- **US-003 — Release-plugin wiring + docs** (`.claude/skills/release-plugin/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/codex-plugins-local.md`): Pre-flight invocation + abort-on-nonzero + line-191 reconcile + doc
  notes. Depends on US-001.

**Ship step (not a story — lead/bookkeeper duty):** after US-001..US-003 land as a commit inside the
`ai-developer-toolkit/` submodule, codexu records the updated `ai-developer-toolkit` submodule pointer
as a separate codexu commit (two-commit flow). This is single-repo implementation (the toolkit
submodule) plus a parent pointer bump — NOT a true dual-repo plan, so `/implement-with-ralph` can drive
the toolkit edits in a toolkit worktree; the lead does the pointer bump at ship time.

## Suggested Decomposition
Three stories, all in the `ai-developer-toolkit` repo. US-001 is the foundation; US-002 and US-003
both depend on it but touch disjoint files, so they may run in parallel in a second phase (or serial —
the total surface is small).

### Cluster: validator-core
- Stories: US-001
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.mjs`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Foundational module every other story imports/invokes; must land first.

### Cluster: fixtures-and-test
- Stories: US-002
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: validator-core
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`tools/fixtures/*.json`, `tools/validate-codex-marketplace-policy.test.mjs`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Test-only files disjoint from the wiring cluster; parallel-safe once the module exists.

### Cluster: release-wiring-and-docs
- Stories: US-003
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: validator-core
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`.claude/skills/release-plugin/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/codex-plugins-local.md`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Doc/skill edits disjoint from the test cluster; parallel-safe once the module exists.

## Open Questions
- **ESM `.mjs` vs CJS `.js`** for the module/test — plan recommends `.mjs` (zero ambiguity, no
  `package.json` needed); impl may choose CJS `.js` to mirror `plugins/crews/tests/*.test.js`. Either
  satisfies the ACs.
- **`.agents/plugins/AGENTS.md`** does not exist; the plan keeps the guard note in root `AGENTS.md` +
  `docs/codex-plugins-local.md` to minimize new files. Adding a short `.agents/plugins/AGENTS.md` is
  an acceptable alternative if preferred.
- **Validate all three indexes vs only the codex index** — plan validates all three (tolerating
  policy-free) so the guard auto-covers a future index that adds `policy`; functionally only the
  codex index is enforced today. Confirm this is the desired breadth.
- Copilot research did not return within its window (non-blocking). The Phase-4 plan review,
  however, completed on all three engines: **Claude** (2 findings: Medium criteria-coverage, Low
  second-policy-free-index — both adopted), **Codex** (1 Critical submodule-pointer-bump + High/Medium
  edge-case findings — all adopted), and **Copilot** (no issues). All findings are resolved in this
  revision (see the Plan Review Findings block below).
